title: The normalized exact derived tensor comparison preserves the native Koszul braiding
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with their fixed K-flat derived tensor structures [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Flat means that tensoring on either side preserves short exact sequences; K-flat complexes and the signed direct-sum total tensor are as in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso].
Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive exact left adjoint with a specified strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], preserving flat objects and K-flat complexes. Write $F_{\rm Ch}$ for its termwise functor and $\tau_{P,Q}:F_{\rm Ch}(P\otimes Q)\cong F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes F_{\rm Ch}Q$ for the direct-sum total comparison induced by the inverse ordinary tensorator. Put $E=D(F)$, let $Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}$ be localization from complexes, and let $\kappa_P:E Q_{\mathcal C}P\cong Q_{\mathcal D}F_{\rm Ch}P$ be the canonical exact-functor factorization.
Let $m_{\mathcal C;P,Q}:Q_{\mathcal C}(P\otimes Q)\cong Q_{\mathcal C}P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_{\mathcal C}Q$ and $m_{\mathcal D}$ be the native K-flat model comparisons. Let $t:E(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)\to EK\otimes^{\mathbf L}EL$ be the natural comparison of [lem-pur-derived-tensor-comparison], normalized for every K-flat pair $P,Q$ by
$$(\kappa_P\otimes\kappa_Q)\circ t_{Q_{\mathcal C}P,Q_{\mathcal C}Q}\circ E(m_{\mathcal C;P,Q})=m_{\mathcal D;FP,FQ}\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{P,Q})\circ\kappa_{P\otimes Q}.$$
Assume also that $F$ respects the ordinary symmetries: writing $c_{A,B}:F(A\otimes B)\cong FA\otimes FB$ for its inverse tensorator, one has
$$c_{B,A}\circ F(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{A,B})=\beta^{\mathcal D}_{FA,FB}\circ c_{A,B}.$$
Give the independently fixed derived tensors their native braidings $\beta^{D(\mathcal C)},\beta^{D(\mathcal D)}$, induced on total complexes by the exchange $(-1)^{pq}\beta$ in bidegrees $(p,q)$. More explicitly, for K-flat $P,Q$ their normalization is
$$\beta^{D(\mathcal C)}_{Q_{\mathcal C}P,Q_{\mathcal C}Q}\circ m_{\mathcal C;P,Q}=m_{\mathcal C;Q,P}\circ Q_{\mathcal C}(\beta^{\rm Ch}_{P,Q}),$$
and similarly for $\mathcal D$. Then for every pair of possibly unbounded derived objects $K,L$,
$$t_{L,K}\circ E(\beta^{D(\mathcal C)}_{K,L})=\beta^{D(\mathcal D)}_{EK,EL}\circ t_{K,L}.$$
This is the braiding equation for the prescribed normalized comparison and the two independently fixed native braidings.

proof.text:
First check the comparison on complexes, without localizing. Write $b_{P,Q}=\beta^{\rm Ch}_{P,Q}$ and suppress the subscript ${\rm Ch}$ on $F$. For $p+q=n$ let $i_{p,q}:P^p\otimes Q^q\to(P\otimes Q)^n$ and $j_{q,p}:Q^q\otimes P^p\to(Q\otimes P)^n$ be the coproduct inclusions of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Since $F$ is a left adjoint, [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] says that the $F(i_{p,q})$ are a coproduct cocone. They therefore determine maps out of $F((P\otimes Q)^n)$ by the uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. On precomposing with $F(i_{p,q})$, the maps $\tau_{Q,P}F(b_{P,Q})$ and $b_{FP,FQ}\tau_{P,Q}$ respectively become
$$j'_{q,p}(-1)^{pq}c_{Q^q,P^p}F(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{P^p,Q^q}),\qquad j'_{q,p}(-1)^{pq}\beta^{\mathcal D}_{FP^p,FQ^q}c_{P^p,Q^q},$$
where $j'$ is the target total-tensor inclusion. Additivity of $F$ moves the sign outside $F$. These expressions are equal by the ordinary braiding hypothesis in the statement. Coproduct uniqueness in every degree proves the equality of cochain maps
$$\tau_{Q,P}\circ F(b_{P,Q})=b_{FP,FQ}\circ\tau_{P,Q}.\tag{*}$$
Only the given bidegree descriptions of $b$ and $\tau$ are used; no new braiding is chosen.

proof.text:
Now let $P,Q$ be K-flat and put $X=Q_{\mathcal C}P$, $Y=Q_{\mathcal C}Q$. By the preservation hypothesis $FP,FQ$ are K-flat too, so all the native model comparisons occurring below are isomorphisms. Abbreviate $m^C_{P,Q}=m_{\mathcal C;P,Q}$, $m^D_{FP,FQ}=m_{\mathcal D;FP,FQ}$, $b=b_{P,Q}$ and $k_{P\otimes Q}=\kappa_{P\otimes Q}$. Precompose the desired equality at $(X,Y)$ with $E(m^C_{P,Q})$ and postcompose with $\kappa_Q\otimes\kappa_P$. For its left side the source native-braiding normalization and then the normalization of $t$ for the reversed pair give
$$\begin{aligned}
&(\kappa_Q\otimes\kappa_P)t_{Y,X}E(\beta^C_{X,Y})E(m^C_{P,Q})\\
&=(\kappa_Q\otimes\kappa_P)t_{Y,X}E(m^C_{Q,P})E(Q_{\mathcal C}(b))\\
&=m^D_{FQ,FP}Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{Q,P})\kappa_{Q\otimes P}E(Q_{\mathcal C}(b))\\
&=m^D_{FQ,FP}Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{Q,P}\circ F(b))\kappa_{P\otimes Q}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last line is exactly naturality of the canonical factorization $\kappa$ at the cochain map $b$, followed by functoriality of $Q_{\mathcal D}$. Here $\beta^C$ denotes the given derived braiding, not the ordinary symmetry.

proof.text:
For the right side of the same conjugated equality, naturality of the given target derived braiding, normalization of $t$, and then its native model formula give
$$\begin{aligned}
&(\kappa_Q\otimes\kappa_P)\beta^D_{EX,EY}t_{X,Y}E(m^C_{P,Q})\\
&=\beta^D_{Q_{\mathcal D}FP,Q_{\mathcal D}FQ}(\kappa_P\otimes\kappa_Q)t_{X,Y}E(m^C_{P,Q})\\
&=\beta^D_{Q_{\mathcal D}FP,Q_{\mathcal D}FQ}m^D_{FP,FQ}Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{P,Q})\kappa_{P\otimes Q}\\
&=m^D_{FQ,FP}Q_{\mathcal D}(b_{FP,FQ}\circ\tau_{P,Q})\kappa_{P\otimes Q}.
\end{aligned}$$
Equation $(*)$ of Step 1 identifies this with the last line of Step 2. Both the precomposing map $E(m^C_{P,Q})$ and the postcomposing map $\kappa_Q\otimes\kappa_P$ are isomorphisms, with inverses obtained by applying the functor and tensor bifunctor to their inverses. Cancelling them proves the required braiding equation at every pair $(Q_{\mathcal C}P,Q_{\mathcal C}Q)$ of K-flat models. This cancellation does not assume that $t$ has already been proved invertible.

proof.text: Finally regard the two sides as natural transformations from the bifunctor $H(K,L)=E(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)$ to $J(K,L)=EL\otimes^{\mathbf L}EK$. They are natural because $t$ is natural by hypothesis and the prescribed braidings are natural. Closedness and symmetry make each fixed-factor tensor functor on $\mathcal C$ a left adjoint; [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] supplies its preservation of all small colimits. All the other hypotheses of [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability] are precisely the given Grothendieck, additive tensor and functorial flat-resolution assumptions. Thus the full subcategory of K-flat complexes in $K(\mathcal C)$ is a left derivability structure for quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the last assertion of [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus] with $n=2$, both categories $K(\mathcal C)$, both localizations $Q^h_{\mathcal C}:K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$ and both subcategories the K-flat complexes. It says that natural transformations between $H$ and $J$ are determined by their components at pairs of localized K-flat objects. The complexes-localization $Q_{\mathcal C}P$ and homotopy-localization $Q^h_{\mathcal C}P$ are canonically identified by the equivalent descriptions in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; naturality identifies their components. Step 3 proves equality at all such pairs, so the two transformations are equal on every pair $K,L$, including unbounded ones.

The last clause of lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus (n=2, Q^h a localization by def-weil-abstract-derived-category) is applied correctly.
